study.title: Real-time planar angiographic cerebral perfusion imaging
study.venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery

imaging.modality_detail: Diagnostic cerebral DSA (Philips Allura XPER FD20/20, 2 fps, 1024x1024 px) captured at runtime via HDMI video splitter and frame-grabber; only posterior-anterior plane analyzed
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral perfusion; ICA angiograms of the skull (anterior-posterior), stroke/thrombectomy patients
imaging.frames_per_sequence: up to 22 images (11 s); shorter runs padded to 22

task.task_description: Real-time computation of planar DSA cerebral perfusion parameter maps (CBF, CBV, TTP, MTT) from video-output duplicated angiograms, comparing Gaussian curve fitting, a 1D CNN predicting curve-fit parameters per pixel, numerical curve feature estimation, and SVD deconvolution with an AIF derived from U-Net segmentation of the ICA C4 segment; computation times compared.
task.clinical_application: Runtime cerebral perfusion assessment during angiography/thrombectomy for stroke

architecture_names: custom convolutional neural network (convolution and linear layers with ReLU)

temporal_evidence.quote: The resulting density series for each pixel was used to fit a Gaussian distribution with four parameters

G1.quote: the lack of similar results in the literature impedes a comparative, absolute validation of any of these planar angiography perfusion estimations

G2.quote: All the images used in neural network training and perfusion map estimation were acquired in a single center using the same angiography machine and software.

G3.quote: angiographic runs tend to be limited in their ability to display parenchymal and venous contrast dynamics due to their shortness of several seconds only

G4.quote: It is not representative of current state-of-the-art physiologic perfusion models and cannot account for geometric limitations of the imaging modality.

G6.quote: systematic evaluation of its added value in clinical decision-making has yet to be performed

other_limitations: Symmetric Gaussian bolus model is physiologically suboptimal and cannot represent arterial-venous overlay
Non-physiological injection pressures during contrast injection
No systematic comparison with tomographic (CT/MR) perfusion
Analysis limited to the posterior-anterior plane
future_work: Systematic optimization of network architecture against training and inference times
Bayesian inference and improved SVD/curve models accounting for vessel overlay
Comparison of angiographic perfusion maps with tomographic counterparts
Faster hardware and optimized processing for more sophisticated analyses
Clinical studies using runtime angiographic perfusion
